paper_title: Do direct detection experiments constrain axionlike particles coupled to electrons?
suggested_experiment_name: Direct detection experiments (XENON1T, LUX, SuperCDMS, Majorana, EDELWEISS-III, GERDA) constraining axionlike particles coupled to electrons
notes: This paper is a CRITICAL ANALYSIS of existing direct detection limits (GERDA, SuperCDMS, EDELWEISS-III, Majorana, XENON1T, XMASS, LUX, PandaX-II), NOT a new experimental measurement. The authors argue that published dark matter ALP-electron coupling limits are NOT self-consistent because ALPs in the keV–MeV mass range decay radiatively into photons on timescales shorter than the age of the universe (τ_a→γγ < 13.8 Gyr). The paper shows that for most of the parameter space claimed by these experiments, the ALPs cannot be dark matter. Additionally, X-ray and gamma-ray astronomy constraints (from NuSTAR, XMM-Newton, INTEGRAL) exclude the parameter space for m_a > 6 keV. Figure 2 displays the excluded regions (dark grey = unstable ALPs, light grey = astrophysical X-ray/gamma-ray constraints), but no NEW numerical limits are presented—only reinterpretation of existing published bounds. The paper does not extract or tabulate new (m_a, g_ae) data points; it critiques the validity of previously published limits.
